newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Mines minister reports on Bre-X saga.
newsitem.headline: Mines minister reports on Bre-X saga.

text.p: Indonesia's Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said on Wednesday the government had suspended an application for contracts of work from Canada's Bre-X to develop its huge Busang gold field because it did not meet certain administrative conditions.
He also criticised the Alberta-based company for amending its existing contract of work without reporting to the mines and energy ministry or seeking its agreement.
Bre-X estimates the Busang property in East Kalimantan province on Borneo island contains at least 57 million ounces of gold.

Sudjana told a parliamentary commission hearing, in a written response to questions, that the government "suspended the processing of the Bre-X application for a contract of work because it did not meet certain administrative conditions set out by the director-general of mining".
He did not elaborate but he was due to answer further questions as the hearing progressed.
Sudjana also criticised Bre-X. He said the government had found that Bre-X amended its contract of work (for the Busang I property) when it registered with the New York Stock Exchange.
Busang I contains an estimated 2.6 million ounces of gold. Bre-X is still waiting for contracts of work covering Busang II and III which contain the bulk of the gold.

Sudjana said Bre-X had not reported to the mines and energy ministry, or sought the minister's approval, during the transfer of shares in the Busang property from Westralian Resource Projects Ltd to Montague Pacific, and from Montague to Bre-X.

Sudjana said the government had advised Bre-X to work with Barrick Gold Corp, also of Canada, because Indonesia wanted to develop Busang soon and considered it an important source of revenue for the country.
The government has recommended a split of 75 percent for Barrick and 25 percent for Bre-X to develop Busang, and has also sought a 10 percent stake for itself in the find.
